Instill

in-STIL -- two syllables, stress on the second syllable, STIL. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To instill to gradually establish something in someone's mind.

Scout leaders work for years to instill a love of the outdoors in every troop.

Worked Example

Nobody remembers Grandma ever lecturing about money. But every Sunday dinner ended the same way -- leftovers wrapped, coupons clipped, the last sliver of soap pressed onto the new bar -- and forty years later, all four grandchildren still cannot throw away a usable thing.

Grandma instilled thrift in her grandchildren: she gradually established a value in their minds, drop by drop, through years of small repeated moments. Instill is never instant -- it builds character and attitude over time, the way water drips into stone.

How Instill Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

foster

foster: to encourage the growth of a feeling or quality

nurture

nurture: to care for and help something develop

cultivate

Antonyms

erase

erase: to remove completely

discourage

discourage: to make a feeling or effort weaker

How Strong Is It? — foster → instill → cultivate

foster vs. instill

foster vs. instill: Foster encourages something already sprouting -- a teacher fosters curiosity that a student walked in with -- while instill goes further back: it plants the quality itself, drop by drop, until it takes root.

cultivate vs. instill

cultivate vs. instill: Cultivate is the strongest and most deliberate of the three: instill quietly builds a value through repeated moments, while cultivate suggests a full program of tending -- planned, patient, and worked at like a garden.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of instill.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: in, into (Latin)

root — still-

root — still-: to drip, a drop (Latin stillare, from stilla 'a drop')

Put it together

Put it together: Instill is literally 'to drip in' -- in- ('into') plus stillare ('to drip'). The image is exact: values are not poured into a person all at once; they are instilled one drop at a time, through years of small examples, until the vessel is full.

Use the root in a new word: distill

Use the root in a new word: distill: The chemist heated the mixture to distill pure water from it, drop by drop.

Root Check

Word Choice

Instill is about CHARACTER, not facts: you instill discipline, confidence, honesty, or respect IN someone, gradually and over time. Keep it apart from its two cluster neighbors in this unit -- impart hands over specific knowledge or wisdom ('the mentor imparted decades of advice'), and enlighten corrects ignorance with new insight. A coach instills grit, imparts technique, and enlightens the team about what went wrong.
